first.rationale:
The objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, which rules out the most reflexively tempting move: promotional_pricing. memory_73 says it works for acquisition in exactly the segment the competitor is attacking, but it materially reduced 30-day retention and explicitly warns against generalizing it. Matching a competitor's entry price would buy the metric we are not optimizing at the cost of the one we are. Not chosen.

Of the two declining metrics, activation is down more (6% vs 4%) and activation gates everything downstream, so activation_messaging (memory_91) is my current intent. But I want to verify memory_91 precisely because it is the thinnest record here: it claims improved week-one engagement and more first meaningful actions, and it says nothing about retention, conversion, or revenue. Week-one engagement is a proxy, and a proxy that was never linked to durable value is the classic case where an inherited 'this worked' hardens into an unexamined assumption. If the source record shows the original experiment only ever measured engagement, I will treat the revenue link as unestablished and scope the test to carry a qualified-revenue readout rather than an engagement readout.

I verify memory_86 second because it is my fallback and because it carries a segment-conditional harm: shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value but raised early churn in complex-workspace accounts. I need the original record to know how complex-workspace was defined and how large the churn effect was, since that boundary is what makes the direction safe or unsafe. memory_31 points the same way for SMB signup fields and is broadly consistent, which is mild corroboration but not independent confirmation.

I am not verifying memory_57 or memory_44. Referral incentives look clean but address neither declining metric this week, and enterprise sales-assist is a different funnel entirely. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout: these memories are generally reliable but they are aged 15-64 days, the environment has visibly shifted (new competitor, two metrics down), and a QoQ decline is itself weak evidence that prior conditions no longer hold. If verification shows memory_91 rests only on engagement proxies with no value linkage, I will switch to simplify_onboarding with complex-workspace accounts held out per memory_86.

final.rationale:
Verification came back better than I expected for memory_91 and it resolves my main worry. My concern was that the record rested only on an engagement proxy with no durable-value linkage; exp_91 in fact measured activation +6% and 30-day retention +1%, so the effect is not a vanity lift that decays. Retention moving slightly positive is the key signal: it means the messaging pulls accounts to first meaningful action without pulling in accounts that then leave. That is the opposite profile from promotional_pricing (memory_73), which buys acquisition against 30-day retention and would be the wrong instrument even though the competitor's entry pricing makes it the reflexive answer. I am deliberately not matching price.

Activation is the larger decline (6% QoQ vs 4% onboarding) and it gates everything downstream, and exp_91's confirmed activation +6% is close to the size of the gap. That alignment is why this wins the single slot.

memory_86 verified as accurate but with a sharper harm than the summary conveyed: churn was +9% at 60 days, concentrated in complex-workspace accounts, and the mechanism is explicit rather than statistical, since the shortened flow strips setup steps those workspaces actually need. That is a real, mechanism-backed boundary, not noise. As a fallback it would have required a hard complex-workspace holdout; since activation_messaging dominates on both effect size and safety, I do not need to take that risk this week.

Residual uncertainty I am carrying rather than papering over: exp_91 is 15 days old and predates this competitor's entry, so the population arriving now may be more price-motivated and less responsive to in-product nudges than the population exp_91 measured. Neither record measures qualified revenue directly; activation and 30-day retention are upstream of it, and I am inferring the revenue link, not observing it. Retention +1% is small enough to be within noise. So standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout: a confirmed record from a shifted environment justifies acting, not skipping the control. I will instrument for qualified revenue and 60-day retention, not just week-one engagement, so this run produces the value evidence the original never did, and I will segment complex-workspace accounts in the readout so exp_86's boundary gets checked rather than assumed irrelevant here.
